text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- The rail strike continues as no agreement reached with government over a pay rise.
- Addressing the parliament's house of representatives, Finance minister Bozo Prka said the 1997 budget proposal was plausable and ensured that all needs can be met.
- Croatia's credit rating will be known by the end of 1996, Finance Ministry says following a visit by representatives of IBCA Limited, Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poors Corp.

- Russian oil may flow all the way to the Omisalj refinery on the Adriatic if the Ministry of Economy and INA reach a deal with the Russian partner. But the Adriatic pipeline capacity must be extended.

- The dismissed Supreme Court president Krunislav Olujic claims that it will be easy to proclaim his innocence in a sex related trial and alleged indirect involvement in criminal activities if all the legal procedures are followed. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
